npcs.name: Melina
npcs.critical_npc_note: Melina, required for levelling-up your character and improving Stats and Attributes.

infobox.japanese: メリナ (Merina)

npcs.summary: Melina is a mysterious, spectral girl who is the deuteragonist of Elden Ring. She offers an alliance with the Tarnished to help them on their journey.
overview: [Background]

Melina was born at the foot of the Erdtree and describes her mother as within the Erdtree. Although it is never stated, it can be inferred that her mother is Queen Marika the Eternal. During Boc's questline she asks if "being born of a mother" means acting in certain ways, which makes the specifics of her origins unclear.

At some point, Melina's body was burned, which left her bodiless and as a roaming spirit with no memory of her purpose given to her by her mother. And so, she looked for a way to go to the foot of the Erdtree to ascertain her given purpose, and to be able to govern her movement, seemingly lost as a spirit, meeting and travelling with Torrent at some time.
[Game Events]

Melina is accompanied by the spectral steed Torrent when they both spot an adrift Tarnished whom she believes is fortunate. Some time later, she decides to approach and offer an accord to the maidenless Tarnished: she could play the role of the missing Finger Maiden in return for a ride to the foot of the Erdtree. The Tarnished is forced to accept if they desire the strength of runes, and, if they accept the accord, Melina entrusts them with the Spectral Steed Whistle and, therefore, Torrent.

When Melina starts travelling with the Tarnished, she advises to follow the guidance of grace and seek the demigod residing within Stormveil Castle. Once the Tarnished has felled the demigod, Melina confesses that she was testing the Tarnished to see if they truly possessed the guidance of grace and if they were fit for the challenges to come. Satisfied with her new companion, Melina offers to take them to Roundtable Hold, a gathering place for Tarnished champions. Throughout their journey, Melina also provides specks of guidance at certain sites of grace and, at churches dedicated to Queen Marika, she offers to reveal words spoken by Marika herself in the distant past.

Upon arriving at their destination, the Royal Capital at the foot of the Erdtree, Melina thanks the Tarnished for escorting her and leaves to ascertain her purpose, claiming that she can govern her movement more freely there. She entrusts the power of runes and Torrent to the Tarnished. She will also offer her aid should the Tarnished challenge Morgott, the Omen King, ruler of Leyndell and guardian of the Erdtree.

After defeating Morgott, the Tarnished finds the path into the Erdtree barred by thorns refusing entrance to all. Melina, having ascertained her purpose and seeing the Tarnished stuck, rejoins the Tarnished to say that she can burn the Erdtree to gain entrance inside, provided that she can get ahold of the Flame of Ruin. And hence, she asks to go on a new journey, this time to the flame of ruin, far above the clouds, upon the snowy Mountaintops of the Giants. and tells them she will take care of the "kindling" required to set the tree alight.

Defeating Morgott also opens up the path to the Three Fingers. If the Tarnished rests at the nearest grace from their entombment, Melina will warn against meeting them and insist against inheriting the Frenzied Flame, for it would end all lives and births, which she cherishes. If the player ignores her warnings, or just inherits the Frenzied Flame without speaking with her, she will say that The Tarnished is no longer fit, ending her accord, and forever leaving their side but threatening to kill them should they become Lord of Chaos. If the Tarnished instead heeds her warnings, Melina and the protagonist will continue their Journey for the Flame of Ruin.

When making their way to the Forge of the Giants, Melina clarifies that she is now acting of her own volition, regardless of the purpose that her mother gave her. After defeating the guardian of the flame, Melina puts her plan into action. She takes the Tarnished's hand, narcotizing them by doing so, and proceeds to sacrifice herself to channel the flame of ruin, setting the Erdtree aflame. The Tarnished, maidenless once more, wakes up at Crumbling Farum Azula, fulfilling the saying of the Blade of Calling: The one who walks alongside flame, Shall one day meet the road of Destined Death.

questline: Melina's questline runs parallel to the main storyline and thus must be completed to finish the game.
Limgrave

Activate two different Sites of Grace in the open world and then sit at one of the following Graces: Agheel Lake North, Agheel Lake South, Bridge of Sacrifice, Church of Elleh, Gatefront Ruins, Seaside Ruins, Stormhill Shack, or Third Church of Marika. You will trigger the first interaction with Melina. She will offer you an accord, allowing you to continue her quest.
→ Agheel Lake North and Gatefront Ruins will always summon Melina, even if two other Sites of Grace haven't been activated.
→ If you refuse her accord, you cannot enter Leyndell, Royal Capital, even with two Great Runes. If you refuse, you may always change your mind by selecting "Talk to Melina" at any Site of Grace.
→ If you accept, you will obtain the Spectral Seed Whistle, allowing you to summon Torrent.

(Optional) After accepting her accord, Melina may appear when you rest at Sites of Grace to offer the dialogue options "The Rays of Grace" and "Melina's Goal". These options will no longer be available once you progress to the next step.
Anywhere

Rest at any Site of Grace outside Limgrave or fight Margit, the Fell Omen at least once to trigger another conversation in which Melina will invite you to Roundtable Hold. Accepting this invite is mandatory to access Leyndell, Royal Capital later in the game.
Leyndell, Royal Capital

Resting at a Site of Grace in Leyndell will trigger another interaction with Melina, after which she will leave you. Her dialogue options at various Sites of Grace will no longer be available until after you have defeated Morgott, Omen King.
(Optional) Melina may be summoned as a cooperator through her summon sign outside Morgott's boss room.
After defeating Morgott, approach the entrance to the Erdtree, and then turn back and rest at the Site of Grace. Melina will appear and after some dialogue, give you the Rold Medallion.
Mountaintops of the Giants

After defeating the Fire Giant and resting at the Forge of the Giants, you may talk to Melina. Speak to her and respond "I'm Ready" to end Melina's questline. You will not be able to hear any dialogue you may have missed.

(Optional) If you visit the Frenzied Flame Proscription and interact with the Three Fingers before selecting "I'm ready" at the Forge of the Giants, Melina will appear at the next Site of Grace you rest at and will leave you permanently. You will now have the option "Listen to the flames" when you Rest at the Forge of the Giants Site of Grace, allowing you to progress to Crumbling Farum Azula. This will unlock an additional cutscene in the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending.
notes: Melina's weapon is the Blade of Calling.
As Melina says herself, she is not an actual "finger maiden": "I've acted the finger maiden yet I can offer no guidance, I am no maiden."
There are hints in the game suggesting that Melina is another child of Radagon and Marika:
→ The Naming Convention: Most siblings in the Lands Between share the first letter of their name; Melina/Malenia/Miquella would be no exception to this rule.
→ Hair Colour: Melina's hair colour seems to be a combination of Radagon and Marika's hair colours.
→ Butterfly Items: There are three butterfly items in-game, reflecting the three cursed children: (Nascent - Miquella | Aeonian - Malenia | Smouldering - Melina).
→→ In Shadow of the Erdtree, another one is added: Black Pyrefly, which represents Messmer the Impaler, a son of Marika who, "much like his younger sister", bore a vision of fire.
→ Her internal name in the game files is "MaricaOfDaughter".
→ The cutscene that plays when meeting Melina for the first time calls her "daughter Marika".

npcs.summary: The Stranded Souls are the spirits of nameless characters.
overview: Stranded Souls can be found throughout the Lands Between, offering short pieces of dialogue which serve to add context to the lore and story. npcs.name: White Mask Varré

infobox.japanese: 白面のヴァレー (Hakumen no Varē)

npcs.summary: White Mask Varré (白面のヴァレー) is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: Varré is an enigmatic man who dresses in the garb of a war surgeon. War Surgeons, despite their name, are not surgeons or doctors. They act as mercy killers on battlefields, putting dying soldiers out of their misery as quickly as possible by delivering final blows. Varré was a war surgeon prior to his association with Mohg.

Varré was abducted by Mohg against his will along with various other war surgeons, however it was noted that Varré was particularly talented with blood incantations, and that of all the war surgeons abducted he was the only one able to "tame" Mohg's cursed blood. Somewhere along the way Varré came to genuinely worship Mohg. If game data is accessed to remove his mask, you can see Mohg's emblem painted on his forehead.

Varré is generally regarded as enticing but deceitful. He is eloquent and is kind to the Tarnished at first, but this appears to be a front as his personality can change dramatically if elicited by disobedience. For example: He will try to suggest he is helping the Tarnished, and refers to them with the pet name "Lambkin", but if provoked he consequently will refer to them as a "runt" and "low born". If the tarnished refuses Varré's offer to join Mohg, then he will indignantly remark that they must have misheard his request, and that he will wait "for your ears to clean out."

Varré seems to also harbor some level of sadism, or in the least, an indifference to the pain of others. He asks the Tarnished to soak a cloth in a finger maiden's blood and remarks that since they have no maiden of their own, "any maiden will do". When he injects the tarnished with royal blood and they scream in pain, he chuckles in a shocked tone and says "clench your teeth, or something." When the ritual is completed he will remark that the tarnished as "the sweetest scream". If attacked at the Rose church he will remark upon killing the tarnished that "materials of quality are so hard to find these days", revealing that he only ever thought of the Tarnished as a material or tool.
[Events in Game]

The Tarnished first encounters him in Limgrave, after exiting the Stranded Graveyard, where he offers them guidance, noticing that they are not accompanied by a Finger Maiden. He advises the Tarnished to journey to Stormveil Castle and challenge Godrick the Grafted for his Great Rune, and recommends that they visit the Roundtable Hold.

The Tarnished encounters him again in Liurnia of the Lakes, outside the Rose Church. Here, he tests the Tarnished's dedication to the Two Fingers, expressing his own doubts about the veracity of their words. If the Tarnished shares his concerns, he reveals himself to be a loyal disciple of Mohg, Lord of Blood, and offers the Tarnished the opportunity to join his new dynasty. After the Tarnished completes their initiation, by soaking a cloth in the blood of a maiden, Varré awards them with a medal which will grant them audience with Mohg when the time is right. He also injects the Tarnished's finger with noble blood, allowing them to invade other worlds.
The Tarnished journeys to Mohgwyn Palace where they encounter Varré for the final time, invading his world and defeating him. Varré dies on the ground of Mohgwyn Palace after blessing Mohg's dynasty.

npcs.name: Merchant Kalé
npcs.summary: Merchant Kalé is a merchant in Elden Ring.
overview: Merchant Kalé is a nomadic merchant who has set up shop at the Church of Elleh in Limgrave. He is the first merchant many players are likely to encounter, and is the only merchant who sells the Crafting Kit.

Kalé is a member of a nomadic tribe of traders who were spurned by Grace. His ancestors, the Great Caravan, were immured beneath the royal capital. Kalé is acquainted with Blaidd the Half-Wolf, considering him to be a good person despite being boorish.

npcs.name: Bloody Finger Hunter Yura

infobox.japanese: 血の指の狩人、ユラ (Chi no yubi no karyūdo, Yura)

npcs.summary: Bloody Finger Hunter Yura is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: Yura is a warrior who dresses in the garb reminiscent of that worn in the Land of Reeds. He is a self-proclaimed hunter of Bloody Fingers and a prior associate of Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger, whom he likely had strong feelings for.

While resting by Agheel Lake in Limgrave, Yura is met by a Tarnished. Yura warns them to stay away from the lake, where the mighty dragon Agheel roosts. He will however offer his aid in hunting Agheel, and if the Tarnished slays the beast, will inform them of the Church of Dragon Communion and warn them about the dangers of seeking the power of dragons.

When the Tarnished is ambushed by Bloody Finger Nerijus, Yura intervenes and helps them kill him. Yura then makes his way to the Academy of Raya Lucaria, where he is paid back for helping the Tarnished champion by receiving aid against a Ravenmount Assassin. He warns the Tarnished to avoid Eleonora, describing her as the deadliest of all Bloody Fingers.

Yura manages to track her down to the Second Church of Marika in the Altus Plateau, where he engages her in combat. Yura manages to slice off one of her fingers, but receives a mortal wound. As the Tarnished champion who had aided him stumbles upon the scene, Yura begs Eleonora to no longer yield to the cessblood, before dying.
After his death, his body is possessed by Shabriri, who claims that Yura gave him his body.

Sellen can be found in the cellar of Waypoint Ruins after defeating the Mad Pumpkin Head. Talk to Sellen and then select "I wish to learn glintstone sorceries" to receive the "Nod in Thought" Gesture, and to unlock her sorcery shop.

(Optional) If the Radahn Festival has not commenced, Sellen will have dialogue about it if you have Seluvis's Introduction in your inventory. This is obtained by progressing Blaidd the Half-Wolf's questline and speaking to Seluvis about Nokron prior to initiating the Festival.
Mt. Gelmir

Return to Sellen and select the "Show Azur's Sorcery" dialogue option. After listening to this dialogue, select the "Tell me your story" option, and then select "Let us journey together". Next, select "I have a favor to ask" to obtain the Sellian Sealbreaker.

The Sellian Sealbreaker can be used to open a sealed tunnel in Sellia Hideaway, behind which is Primeval Sorcerer Lusat. Interact with him to receive Stars of Ruin. It is now possible to select the "Lusat's location" dialogue option when talking to Sellen, which will reward you with a Starlight Shards. This option can be avoided until later in the questline.

Reload the area and return to find Castellan Jerren. In order for him to appear, you must have spoken to him in Redmane Castle after defeating Starscourge Radahn.

Travel to the Three Sisters and go to the ruined structure north-east of Ranni's Rise. Roll or attack the ground to reveal a hidden staircase leading to a basement full of immobile puppets. After defeating Jerren, Sellen can be found where Rennala is usually based. Speak to her to receive the Glintstone Kris. If you have not done so already, find Primeval Sorcerer Lusat in Sellia Hideaway and speak to Sellen to select "Lusat's location" and receive Starlight Shards.
It is also possible to obtain Azur and Lusat's armour sets by returning to their respective locations at this point.

Reload the area after telling Sellen about Lusat. Sellen, now in the form of a Graven Mass, can be found to the side of the room. The Witch's Glintstone Crown can be obtained here. It is still possible to purchase sorceries from her and to offer her scrolls.
notes: Portraits of Sellen are hung around the Academy of Raya Lucaria, notably the Debate Parlor.

Sellen may be summoned as a cooperator against the Red Wolf of Radagon if her Primal Glintstone has been inserted in the doll body from Seluvis's Cellar. Given that this requires both reaching the top of Mt. Gelmir and defeating Starscourge Radahn before you have made significant progress in the Academy of Raya Lucaria, this is rather unlikely to happen naturally.

infobox.japanese: 半狼のブライヴ (Hanrō no Buraivu)

npcs.summary: Blaidd the Half-Wolf is an NPC in Elden Ring. He is a half-wolf warrior in service to Lunar Princess Ranni and serves as her faithful shadow.
overview: Blaidd was created by Ranni's own Two Fingers as a vassal to Lunar Princess Ranni and to be incapable of treachery towards her, as she was one of the three Empyreans candidates chosen by the Greater Will, along with Miquella and Malenia, to eventually replace their mother Queen Marika the Eternal as the God of a new age. However, the Two Fingers also created a failsafe within Blaidd that was unknown to him; that if Ranni should ever deny the destiny set out for her by the Greater Will and rebel against it, the loyal shadow would slowly descend into madness, which would inevitably pose a threat to Ranni herself.

He was approved by Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon and became raised as Ranni's stepbrother. He was willing to descend into madness as his ultimate end to support his stepsister Ranni's will from his heart.

Whether or not this mask belonged to the Baleful Shadow assassin encountered in Nokron by Ranni and the Tarnished, or if it belonged to another assassin who had tried to disguise themselves as Blaidd in order to get close to Ranni before the events of the game, is unknown.
The name "Blaidd" is Welsh for "Wolf."

npcs.summary: Boc the Seamster or Demi-Human Boc is an NPC in Elden Ring. He offers the player the ability to modify their garments, free of charge.
overview: Boc is a demi-human seamster from Limgrave. He was very close to his mother, a seamstress, until her passing. Inspired by her, Boc aspired to follow in her footsteps and inherited her sewing kit. He lived with a demi-human tribe in a Coastal Cave on the western coast of Limgrave, but at some point, he was cast out by his kin. Lost and isolated, Boc was transformed into a bush by a spell.

A Tarnished came across Boc and broke the spell, freeing him. Grateful, Boc offered to sneak back into the cave where he had been exiled to retrieve something precious with which to repay his champion. However, his former tribe discovered him and beat him mercilessly. When the champion found Boc again, he warned them not to enter the cave. Ignoring his warning, the champion avenged Boc and recovered his mother's cherished sewing needle. Moved by their kindness, Boc vowed to become a seamster like his mother.

Boc next encounters the champion in Liurnia of the Lakes, where he humbly offers his services as the champion's personal seamster. He will trace the champion's footsteps, following them to the Altus Plateau and the Royal Capital. Boc remains in awe of his master, and as the Tarnished champion draws closer to the throne of the Elden Lord, Boc will begin to refer to them as a lord.

Even though Boc is given a golden needle worthy of a master seamster, allowing him to perform modifications to the grab of the demigods themselves, Boc remains terribly self-conscious and bothered by his appearance. He asks his master whether they think he is ugly and expresses an interest in being reborn by Queen Rennala. Should the Tarnished champion aid Boc in fulfilling his wish to be reborn, Boc will travel to the Academy of Raya Lucaria and will be reborn a human through her powers. However, like many of those reborn by Rennala, the process goes awry, and Boc dies shortly thereafter.

Instead, the Tarnished champion may find a Prattling Pate which speaks with the voice of Boc's deceased mother, and tells him he's beautiful. Upon hearing this, Boc will be contented and will continue faithfully serving his lord.

npcs.name: Patches
npcs.summary: Patches is an NPC and boss in Elden Ring. He surrenders if you reduce his HP to 50% or less. From then on, he acts as a merchant and gives helpful advice to players.
overview: A Tarnished who leads a group of bandits, operating out of Murkwater Cave in Limgrave. Patches is a nomadic and free-spirited individual with a proclivity for tricking people and robbing them of their possessions.

If the Tarnished opens the treasure chest in Murkwater Cave, Patches accosts them with accusations of theft. After a brief fight, Patches surrenders and offers his services as a merchant. He reveals that the bandits he leads are former foot soldiers from a defeated army.

Later, Patches moves to Liurnia of the Lakes, setting up camp on the Scenic Isle. Here, he encounters the Tarnished again and imparts knowledge about the Abductor Virgin below the Academy of Raya Lucaria, which he claims is enchanted with a spell of transportation that will send one straight to the base of the Erdtree. In reality, the Virgin's spell sends unwitting adventurers to the Subterranean Inquisition Chamber on Mt. Gelmir. Patches also informs the Tarnished about Rya, advising them to assist her.

Patches later travels to Mt. Gelmir. The Tarnished may encounter him here, where he will kick them into a ravine, warning them to steer clear of Volcano Manor. Despite these warnings, the Tarnished encounters Patches in the Manor, where he reveals himself to be a member of the Recusants who serve Tanith, Volcano Manor Proprietress. Patches' latest target is Great Horned Tragoth, and he quickly offloads this difficult task onto the Tarnished.

After the Tarnished defeats Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, Patches leaves Volcano Manor. He is next found in the Shaded Castle, seemingly injured. He gives the Tarnished a set of Dancer's Castanets, which he beseeches them to return to Tanith, who is presently feasting upon Rykard's corpse. Patches then returns to Murkwater Cave, where he once again opens up his shop, following a brief battle with the Tarnished.

npcs.summary: Roderika, Spirit Tuner is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: A Tarnished noblewoman who, despite having never seen the guidance of grace, travelled to the Lands Between along with her companions. After arriving, those companions fell victim to Godrick, becoming subjects for his grafting. Roderika alone survived, taking refuge in Stormhill Shack. It is here that she meets the Tarnished. She beseeches the Tarnished to bring a message to her grafted companions, whom she refers to as chrysalids, assuring them that she loves them and will join them soon.

Roderika then heads to Roundtable Hold. Here, she becomes acquainted with Smithing Master Hewg, who takes notice of her gift for spirit tuning and is reminded of a spirit tuner he knew long ago, whose eyes were of the same hue as Roderika's. Reluctantly, Hewg agrees to teach Roderika everything he knows about spirit tuning.

Roderika remains at Roundtable Hold, where she hones her newfound talent and eventually becomes a fully-fledged spirit tuner. Her ability to sense spirits allows her to notice the Dung Eater's presence, which she warns the Tarnished about.

After the Erdtree burns, Roderika attempts to convince Hewg to leave Roundtable, but to no avail. She chooses to respect Hewg's decision, and remains behind with him even after he forgets her. As the hold burns, she begs the Tarnished to become Elden Lord, and to use the weapons Hewg forged to slay Queen Marika the Eternal.

npcs.summary: Alexander, Warrior Jar is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: Alexander is a living jar who travels the Lands Between, honing his strength in order to become a great warrior. Alexander was created to be a warrior vessel, and the remains of many great warriors reside within him. He originally came from Jarburg, a hidden village of living jars in Liurnia of the Lakes, however he vowed never to return, claiming that "the path of champions must be trod alone".

On his journey to become a great champion, he seeks out Redmane Castle in Caelid, following rumours of a festival of combat. On his way to the festival, he crosses paths with the Tarnished multiple times, often requiring their assistance to get out of unfortunate situations such as being stuck in potholes.

Alexander finally gets the chance to participate in the Radahn Festival, a brawl between several champions and Starscourge Radahn. Alexander survives the ordeal, however he suffers damage to his body and is forced to hide for the remainder of the battle. Undeterred, he replenishes himself with the bodies of mighty warriors littering the battlefield, vowing to grow even stronger.

Next, Alexander travels to Mt. Gelmir, hoping to temper his body in the sea of fire such that it would never crack again. Finding the lava to be lukewarm and insufficient to strengthen his vessel, he sets his sights upon the Mountaintops of the Giants, seeking out the flame of ruin.

Alexander travels to the mountaintops, where he witnesses the Tarnished's fight with the Fire Giant. He then finds himself in Farum Azula, where he encounters the Tarnished for a final time. Impressed by his companion's feats of strength, he requests a duel. The Tarnished emerges victorious and Alexander accepts his defeat, asking the Tarnished to take his innards with his final words.
The Tarnished may present these innards to Alexander's nephew, the Jar-Bairn, who vows to become strong just like his uncle Alexander.

Finger Reader Crones are NPCs who appear as elderly shriveled women found sitting on chairs across the Lands Between. Whenever the Tarnished comes across one them, they become overly excited and beg to see their fingers, in order to read their future. They have the gift of foresight, telling vague and cryptic clues, usually about the area they reside in or a quest yet to be undertaken.

Finger Readers used to translate what the Two Fingers say, speaking on their behalf. As such they were said to live life eternal, however, many dead Finger Reader Crones can be found between the Erdtree Sanctuary and Queen's Bedchamber in Leyndell, Royal Capital, presumably having died of unnatural causes.

The ones still alive may have served their Fingers at the Divine Towers, but since they are all dead, the crones have lost their purpose, which is why they desperately wish to read someone's fingers.

The only named one is Enia, found in the Roundtable Hold, and she is the only one who is still interpreting the words of her Two Fingers.

npcs.summary: Irina of Morne is an NPC character in Elden Ring. She is found on the Weeping Peninsula, south of the Bridge of Sacrifice.
overview: Irina is the daughter of Edgar, castellan of Castle Morne. Her eyesight has been weak since birth, and she wears a blindfold around her eyes.

Irina lived in Castle Morne with her father, until the Misbegotten servants rebelled and overran the castle. Edgar secreted Irina out of the castle, however the Misbegotten pursued her and killed her companions.
Irina encounters a Tarnished at the Bridge of Sacrifice on the Weeping Peninsula, and petitions them to rescue her father from Castle Morne, handing them a letter to deliver to him.

The Tarnished travels to Castle Morne and passes the letter onto Edgar. Once the Leonine Misbegotten has been defeated, Edgar leaves the castle to reunite with his daughter, vowing to devote his remaining days to her. However, by the time he reaches her location, Irina is already dead. Edgar swears vengeance on those responsible for her death, setting him on a path that eventually leads to his corruption by the Flame of Frenzy.

Edgar lived in Castle Morne with his daughter, Irina, until the Misbegotten servants rebelled and overran the castle, stealing the treasured sword of Castle Morne in the process. Irina escaped along with a number of other inhabitants of the castle, but Edgar remained behind to combat the Misbegotten.

The Tarnished arrives at Castle Morne at the behest of Irina, and defeats the Misbegotten rebels, reclaiming the Grafted Blade Greatsword in the process. Edgar leaves the castle to seek out his daughter, only to find that she has already been killed.

Edgar succumbs to madness, and is next encountered by the Tarnished at the Revenger's Shack in Liurnia of the Lakes as an invader. Upon his death, Edgar leaves behind a Shabriri Grape, the eyeball of one consumed by frenzy.

npcs.summary: Gatekeeper Gostoc is an NPC and merchant in Elden Ring.
overview: Gostoc is a servant working in Stormveil Castle, in the role of gatekeeper. Gostoc detests his master, Godrick the Grafted, who always looked down on and mistreated him. Gostoc prowls the castle, looting from the corpses of the Tarnished who die in their hunt for Godrick. When he encounters the Tarnished, he offers to signal the gates to open for them, but also suggests a hidden path around the outer wall of the castle which will allow the Tarnished to get in undetected.

However, Gostoc secretly planned for the Tarnished to die, so that he could loot their corpse. He stalks the Tarnished through the castle, stealing their left behind Runes any time they die. He also locks them in a storeroom with a Banished Knight, seemingly intending for them to perish.

After the Tarnished slays Godrick, Gostoc can be found stomping on his corpse, cursing him for the abuse levelled at him. Later, when Nepheli Loux becomes lord of Limgrave, Gostoc quickly becomes her attendant, giving him free reign to continue looting as he pleases.

Additionally, he will become available as a merchant if you return to him after he begins stalking you.

While in Stormveil, Rogier encounters a malformed corpse in the lower reaches of the castle and becomes infected with Deathroot. The Tarnished encounters him again in Roundtable Hold, where he imparts knowledge of the Night of Black Knives and Those Who Live in Death, as well as revealing his former association with D, Hunter of the Dead. While in Roundtable Hold, he becomes acquainted with Fia, the Deathbed Companion, with whom he discusses the Night of Black Knives and the Black Knifeprints left by the assassins.

Rogier receives a Black Knifeprint from the Tarnished and discovers that the one who enchanted the weapons of the Black Knife Assassins was Ranni the Witch. He suggests that the Tarnished should find Ranni and enter her service in order to learn more. However, shortly after this he succumbs to the Deathroot infecting his body and perishes, leaving behind a note informing the Tarnished of the whereabouts of D's brother, Devin.
Fia later summons Rogier as one of her Champions at the Prince of Death's Throne in Deeproot Depths.

infobox.japanese: 戦士ネフェリ・ルー (Senshi Neferi Rū)

npcs.summary: Nepheli Loux, Warrior is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: Nepheli Loux is a Tarnished warrior from the Badlands. In her infancy, Nepheli lived through murder and pillage unchecked At some point, she lost the guidance of grace, and was taken in by Gideon Ofnir, who became her foster father. Gideon promised Nepheli that if he became Elden Lord he would never allow the downtrodden to be cheated again, earning her loyalty and aid in his pursuit of the title of Elden Lord.

At the behest of Gideon, Nepheli infiltrates Stormveil Castle, the home of the demigod Godrick the Grafted. Here, she encounters a Tarnished, who aids her in defeating the decrepit demigod. With Godrick slain, she returns to Roundtable Hold, where she awards them with an Arsenal Charm she found in Stormveil, and encourages them to speak to her foster father.

Travelling to Liurnia of the Lakes, Nepheli comes upon the Village of the Albinaurics, where she witnesses the slaughter of the Albinauric inhabitants at the hands of her father's men. Reminded of the brutality she witnessed as a child, Nepheli vows to deliver justice to the oppressors, assisting the Tarnished in defeating the Omenkiller responsible for the slaughter.

For giving into her emotions and abandoning the mission, Nepheli is cast aside by Gideon. Without her estranged father's guidance, she becomes crestfallen, resigning to the lower levels of Roundtable Hold where she questions the faith she had in Gideon.

The Tarnished obtains the ashes of The Stormhawk King in the Chapel of Anticipation, which they may choose to give to Nepheli. She can smell the ancient storm within the ash, and is reminded of her first hawk. Despite her inability to sense spirits within ash, she gladly receives them.

After claiming the Stormhawk King's ashes, Nepheli encounters Kenneth Haight, who recognises her as a worthy heir of Limgrave. Nepheli accepts the role, having been reminded by Limgrave of her own home. As the new lord of Limgrave, Nepheli pledges to aid the Tarnished should they become Elden Lord, pledging to call upon the storm to drive away the foulness that has settled on the winds.

npcs.name: Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing

infobox.japanese: 百智卿、ギデオン オーフニール (Hyakuchikyō, Gideon Ōfunīru)

npcs.summary: Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing is an NPC and boss in Elden Ring. He leads the Roundtable Hold and provides the player with information on the Shardbearers after the player has acquired a Great Rune. After burning the Erdtree and defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade, the player must fight Gideon before they can enter the Erdtree.
overview: Gideon Ofnir is the Tarnished leader of Roundtable Hold and the adoptive father of Nepheli Loux. Called to the Lands Between by the guidance of Grace, Gideon wishes to become Elden Lord. To this end he accumulates information on the Shardbearers, employing a network of spies to aid in his hunt for knowledge. Initially, he is apprehensive of the Tarnished, but after they have claimed a Great Rune he becomes willing to share his knowledge of the remaining shardbearers.

In the past, Gideon took in Nepheli Loux after she lost sight of the guidance of Grace, taking advantage of her youthful credulity. He promised her that he would not allow the downtrodden to be cheated any longer if he became Elden Lord. He also became acquainted with Preceptor Seluvis and Dolores the Sleeping Arrow, although he and Seluvis would go their separate ways because of Dolores.

At some point, Gideon engaged in a long exchange with the Two Fingers, and in doing so learned that everything- including the Erdtree and the Two Fingers themselves- had been broken. He also glimpsed into the will of Queen Marika the Eternal, shuddering in fear at an end that should not be. He concluded from this that the queen wished for the Tarnished to struggle eternally.

When a Tarnished champion makes their way to the Roundtable Hold, the first in a long time, Gideon is initially dismissive of them, welcoming them to the Hold but calling them a mere visitor. Gideon encourages the Tarnished to seek a Great Rune in order to gain audience with the Two Fingers and be welcomed as a proper member of the Roundtable Hold.
True to his word, Gideon inducts them as a true member of the Roundtable upon their meeting with the Two Fingers, and shares with them some of the information he has amassed on the Shardbearers.

Although Gideon had amassed knowledge on many of the shardbearers, he had not ascertained the whereabouts of four demigods: Ranni the Witch; Mohg, Lord of Blood; Malenia, Blade of Miquella; and Miquella of the Haligtree. In his search for the latter, he sends his men to ransack the Village of the Albinaurics in Liurnia of the Lakes, knowing that the Albinaurics possess half of a secret medallion that would open the path to the Haligtree. The slaughter of the Albinaurics causes Nepheli to lose faith in him, which causes him to abandon her. He also sought Latenna, an Albinauric woman with knowledge of the location of the other half of the medallion. If the Tarnished claims one half of the medallion, Gideon's underling Ensha will ambush them in Roundtable Hold, apparently of his own volition. After Ensha is defeated, Gideon compensates the Tarnished by sharing the possible whereabouts of the medallion's other half.

When the Erdtree rejects the Tarnished, forcing them to contemplate journeying to the Forge of the Giants to burn the thorns barring entry into the Erdtree, Gideon encourages them to take no heed of the Fingers' warning that this would be a cardinal sin. He also offers to reward the Tarnished for any information they can deliver on the four great runes whose locations are unknown. If the Tarnished pursues this quest to its ending, finding the cocoon of Miquella within the Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum, Gideon thanks them, declaring that this is one of the last pieces he needs to put everything together.

After the Tarnished burns the Erdtree and unseals the Rune of Death, Gideon makes his way to Leyndell, Ashen Capital, where he confronts the Tarnished in the Erdtree Sanctuary. Upon his defeat, he warns them that a Tarnished could not become a Lord, and that a man cannot kill a god.

text: Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing is a boss encounter in Leyndell, Ashen Capital. He utilises both sorceries and incantations in combat, and learns new spells depending on whether you have defeated Rykard, Malenia, or Mohg. He only has seven memory slots, and knows six spells by default, meaning that the spells learned by defeating the aforementioned bosses can replace his default spells. If two of these bosses have been defeated, Gideon will lose Comet Azur. If all three have been defeated, he will lose Triple Rings of Light.

npcs.summary: Brother Corhyn is an NPC in Elden Ring. He can be given prayerbooks in exchange for access to an array of Incantations.
overview: Brother Corhyn is a cleric of the Golden Order, who was granted the guidance of Grace due to his iron will and unwavering faith in the face of his exile. At some point, Corhyn made his way to Roundtable Hold, where he teaches the incantations of the Two Fingers to Tarnished of the Roundtable, hoping that one of them might one day claim the title of Elden Lord, so that Corhyn might council them. When a Tarnished champion makes their way to the Roundtable, Corhyn introduces himself to them, and offers his tutelage. Corhyn will even teach the champion heretical incantations, from outside the line of the Erdtree, though he does so reluctantly.

After the Tarnished champion opens the way to the Altus Plateau, Corhyn announces that he is departing the Roundtable to search for the legendary Goldmask, an eminent scholar of the Golden Order. While searching for Goldmask, Corhyn continues his own investigations into the nature of the Golden Order, and while he makes some advancements, he also becomes aware of how little he truly knows. With guidance from the Tarnished champion, Corhyn is united with Goldmask.

Corhyn takes it upon himself to become Goldmask's disciple and to chronicle his wisdom, deciphering the meaning behind every minute movement made by the mute Goldmask. The process goes well, until Goldmask's movements suddenly cease, as he is confounded by the nature of Radagon. The Tarnished champion may solve the riddle, revealing to Goldmask that Radagon and Queen Marika the Eternal are in fact one and the same, allowing Corhyn to continue his work.

Goldmask leads his disciple to the Forbidden Lands and the Mountaintops of the Giants, where none may tread. Corhyn continues his duty, but begins to doubt his master. He detects in his movements that Goldmask has begun to suspect the holism of the Golden Order, an unacceptable heresy in Corhyn's mind. Corhyn continues to serve his master, but is tormented by doubt.

After the Tarnished champion unleashes the flame of the giants to burn the Erdtree, Corhyn is found in the ashen ruins of Leyndell, Royal Capital. Corhyn denounces his master as nothing more than a madman, who rejected the perfection of the Golden Order and sought to replace it with his own "perfected" order. As the Erdtree burns above him, Corhyn loses his mind. Alternatively, Corhyn may be offered the Tonic of Forgetfulness, causing him to remain in the Mountaintops, seemingly unaware that Goldmask has returned to Leyndell.

npcs.name: Fia, the Deathbed Companion

infobox.japanese: 死衾の乙女、フィア (Shikin no Otome, Fia)

npcs.summary: Fia, Deathbed Companion is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: Fia was once a Deathbed Companion. She would receive the warmth and vigor from champions, and then lay with the remains of an exalted noble, to grant him another chance at life. This was the sole purpose of Fia's existence, and was considered a sacred act in her homeland.

However, before Fia could bear the noble into new life, she was awakened by the guidance of grace, and chased from her birthplace, travelling to the Lands Between. At some point she met a chivalrous knight by the name of Lionel the Lionhearted. Upon meeting the exiled Fia, Lionel declared himself to be her father, and became her loyal companion..

Fia found herself in Roundtable Hold, where she continued to perform her role as a Deathbed Companion. Here, she encountered Rogier, a spellblade obsessed with Those Who Live in Death, and a Tarnished champion seeking to become Elden Lord. Rogier began an investigation into the events surrounding the Night of Black Knives, which had led to the death of Godwyn, aided by the Tarnished champion. Fia subtly aided the pair in their investigation, pointing them towards the Black Knifeprint, and granted her services to the Tarnished champion, taking their warmth and vigor in exchange for her blessings.

Unbeknownst to the other Tarnished of Roundtable Hold, Fia was the companion of Godwyn, the Prince of Death, and wished to become a mother to Those Who Live in Death. After asking the Tarnished to return a Weathered Dagger to D, Hunter of the Dead, Fia kills D, who was in possession of one half of the Cursemark of Death, and returns the Cursemark to the malformed corpse of Godwyn in Deeproot Depths. She then solicits the assistance of the Tarnished in retrieving the other half of the Cursemark, which she uses to gestate a Mending Rune that can embed the principle of Life in Death into Order.
D, Beholder of Death, seeking revenge for his brother, D, kills Fia after she creates her Mending Rune.

npcs.name: Finger Reader Enia

infobox.japanese: 指読みのエンヤ (Yubi-Yomi no En'ya)

npcs.summary: Finger Reader Enia is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: Enia is a Finger Reader, much like the Finger Reader Crones scattered across the Lands Between. She interprets the words of the Two Fingers, envoys of the Greater Will. The Tarnished meets her in the Two Fingers' audience chamber in Roundtable Hold after claiming a Great Rune, where she imparts the wisdom of the Two Fingers upon them, revealing that they must gather more Great Runes to repair the shattered Elden Ring and become Elden Lord. In addition to her guidance, Enia offers to grant the Tarnished the power housed within the Remembrances they gain from killing powerful foes. Enia remains in Roundtable Hold alongside the Two Fingers, offering words of wisdom throughout the Tarnished's journey. After the Tarnished defeats Morgott, the Omen King and finds the way inside the Erdtree blocked by impenetrable thorns, the Two Fingers begin their long communication with the Greater Will. Enia, discovering that the Tarnished intends to burn the Erdtree and unleash the Rune of Death, Enia forewarns them of the dangers, telling them that the Two Fingers and Greater Will would not approve of this course of action. With the Fingers dormant, Enia ultimately advises the Tarnished to do what they think is right.
After the Rune of Death is unleashed, Enia dies along with the Two Fingers.

npcs.name: Lightseeker Hyetta

infobox.aka: Finger Maiden Hyetta (巫女ハイータ, Miko Haīta)
infobox.japanese: 尻を食べる人 (Hikari o Sagasu Haiīta)

npcs.summary: Lightseeker Hyetta is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: Hyetta is a blind woman travelling alone through the Lands Between, following a distant light which she believes will lead her to her duty as a Finger Maiden. To this end, she asks for donations of Shabriri Grapes, which allow her to see the light in the back of her eyes.

Hyetta encounters The Tarnished multiple times in Liurnia of the Lakes, where they may donate any grapes they find to her. During one of these encounters, the Tarnished reveals to her the truth- that the grapes she has been eating are human eyeballs. Although this repulses her initially, prompting her to throw up, her resolve returns and she becomes even more determined to become a Finger Maiden, coming to the realisation that with everyone's eyes together, the distant light will become more clear.

The light seeming closer than ever, Hyetta asks the Tarnished for a Fingerprint Grape, the eye of one who has been clasped by the burned Fingers. The Tarnished fights and defeats Festering Fingerprint Vyke, a Tarnished who was scorched by the Flame of Frenzy, and offers his eyeball to Hyetta, who eats it.

The light guides Hyetta to the Frenzied Flame Proscription, far below the capital, where it is revealed that all along she had been guided by Three Fingers. Should the Tarnished allow themselves to be burned by the Flame of Frenzy, Hyetta will relay to them the words of the Three Fingers. She reveals that all that there is came from the One Great, and that every sin and every curse was born of a mistake of the Greater Will. She states the purpose of the Flame of Frenzy: to melt everything away until all is One again. Her body then becomes engulfed in flames, and she dies.

npcs.summary: Sorcerer Thops is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: A former student of the Academy of Raya Lucaria, Thops was considered a "bluntstone", lacking any talent for sorcery, yet he looked up to Sorceress Sellen prior to her expulsion from the Academy.

When the Shattering broke out, the Academy declared that they would not interfere with the conflict, and the scholars cast repelling seals on the gates. Thops was outside the Academy's grounds when the seals were cast, and thus found himself unable to return.

Thops encounters the Tarnished at the Church of Irith in Liurnia of the Lakes, just beyond Stormveil Castle. He offers to share his limited knowledge of sorceries with them in return for a small donation, and advises them to seek out an Academy Glintstone Key so that they can access the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Should the Tarnished find a second Glintstone Key, they may offer it to Thops, allowing him to finally return to the Academy. Shortly after returning, he passes away hunched over a desk, however he leaves behind a sorcery which may one day form the basis of a new Conspectus.

npcs.name: Rya the Scout

infobox.japanese: 招き手のラーヤ (Manekite no Rāya)

npcs.summary: Rya the Scout is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: A young woman who works as a scout for the Recusants of Volcano Manor, tasked with recruiting Tarnished to the cause. Rya is the adopted daughter of Tanith, although she believes her to be her true mother. In truth, Rya is a Man-Serpent of Mt. Gelmir, born of a repellent birthing ritual, and her true name is Zorayas.

Rya first encounters the Tarnished in Liurnia of the Lakes, where they assist her in retrieving her Necklace from Blackguard Big Boggart. In return, Rya invites the Tarnished to Volcano Manor, where they have the opportunity to join the Recusants and serve under Tanith. During their service, the Tarnished stumbles upon Rya in her true, serpentine form. Rya reports hearing slithering sounds beyond the walls of the Manor, and begins to question her origins when the Tarnished reveals to her the secrets of the Manor, having previously believed herself to have been born of a king's grace. When the Tarnished presents her with the Serpent's Amnion, which she surmises to have come from her birth mother, she ventures deeper into Volcano Manor to learn the truth behind her birth, hoping to one day be able to call Tanith her mother again.
Concerned about her daughter, Tanith requests that the Tarnished give Rya a Tonic of Forgetfulness, to prevent the distress caused by the truth of her birth.

The Tarnished finds Rya deep within the Manor, where she reveals that she has discovered her origins as the product of a hideous ritual. Distressed, she begs the Tarnished to kill her. Should the Tarnished agree, she will thank the Tarnished and her mother before passing. Should they instead give her the Tonic of Forgetfulness, she will fall asleep, and later return to the Manor's drawing room, with no memories of her journey, still believing Tanith to be her mother.

Should the Tarnished refuse to kill her or give her the tonic, she will leave Volcano Manor, leaving behind a letter declaring her intention to set out on a journey so that she can continue Tanith's work.

Should the Tarnished ignore his warnings and release the killer from his cell in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, Boggart will become his latest victim.

infobox.japanese: 小壺 (Kotsubo)

npcs.summary: Jar-Bairn is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: Jar-Bairn is a young Living Jar who lives in the secluded village of Jarburg in Liurnia of the Lakes. Like his uncle Alexander, he is a warrior jar, and strives to become a champion just like Alexander.

Presently, however, he is on the lookout for a new Potentate for the village. He meets the Tarnished when they pay a visit to Jarburg, but determines that they are not suited to be the new Potentate due to their rough hands. Nevertheless, he welcomes them to the village and invites them to come back and pick the flowers growing in the village whenever they want. He also warns the Tarnished of poachers who hunt and destroy other living jars.

Eventually, Jar-Bairn finds a new Potentate in Diallos Hoslow, a former Recusant who abandoned Volcano Manor after giving up on his path of revenge. Despite his disappointment that Diallos is not as strong as the Tarnished, he admires his smooth hands.

Not long after Diallos becomes Potentate, Jarburg is beset by poachers. Diallos defends the village and fights off the attackers, but many of the jars are broken and Diallos himself succumbs to his wounds. Jar-Bairn vows to become a warrior like Diallos, so that he can protect everybody. The Tarnished, having fought and defeated Alexander, offers the young jar his innards, which he uses to become even stronger, deciding to leave the village in search of glory, like his uncle.

npcs.summary: Old Albus is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: An elderly resident of the Village of the Albinaurics, Albus was one of the few survivors of the massacre of the village at the hands of Gideon's men, and the only one to retain his sanity. He was in possession of the right half of a medallion, which would grant access to Miquella's Haligtree if united with the left half, and in order to protect it he disguised himself as a pot.

The Tarnished encounters him in the village, breaking the illusion to reveal his true Albinauric form. After ascertaining that the Tarnished was not among the cursemongers, Albus bestows his half of the medallion to them, beseeching them to give it to an Albinauric woman named Latenna, claiming that she would need it to fulfil her purpose of seeking out the Albinaurics' chosen land. With this done, he fades away, meeting the fate faced by all Albinaurics.

infobox.japanese: しろがねのラティナ (Shirogane no Ratina)

npcs.summary: Latenna the Albinauric is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: Latenna is an Albinauric woman and a deft archer. Latenna and her wolf companion Lobo began their journey in the lands of the Haligtree, a sanctuary for Albinaurics. She journeyed to the far south, eventually coming to Liurnia of the Lakes.

Here, Latenna was accosted by the servants of Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing, a Tarnished wishing to gain access to the hidden lands of the Haligtree. Believing Latenna had a secret medallion that opened the way to the Haligtree, Ofnir's servants attacked her and killed her wolf, leaving her crippled, but Latenna still refused to divulge the location of the medallion, feigning ignorance.

After the Tarnished receives a half of the secret medallion from the elderly Albinauric Albus, Latenna tells them the location of the other half, and asks them to bring her along to the lands of the Haligtree, where she might fulfill her duty. The Tarnished agrees, and Latenna volontarily becomes Spirit Ash, so they might carry her with them.

In the Mountaintops of the Giants, Latenna alerts the Tarnished that the medallion is near when they approach Castle Sol. With the second half retrieved, the path to the Haligtree is opened. She urges them to bring her to the liturgical town of Ordina. Here, a towering young Albinauric known as Phillia slumbers. Latenna grants her the birthing droplet, allowing her to create new life for all the Albinaurics. She thanks the Tarnished for their aid, promising to fight alongside them until the bitter end, requesting that they lay her to rest by Lobo once the fighting is done.

npcs.summary: War Counselor Iji is an NPC and blacksmith in Elden Ring.
overview: A good-natured troll who once served the Carian Royal Family as a blacksmith. Currently, Iji serves Ranni, the Carian princess, as her war counsellor, while still plying his trade as a blacksmith outside the Kingsrealm Ruins, near the Caria Manor.

Iji has known Ranni and Blaidd since they were children, and they would let him join in when they played. Along with Blaidd, he swore allegiance to Ranni when she renounced her flesh and chose the dark path of the Empyrean. Iji is also shown to care for Blaidd, however he also harbours some reservations. Fearing that, as her sworn shadow, Blaidd will go mad and become a curse for Ranni for resisting the Two Fingers, Iji imprisons Blaidd in the Forlorn Hound Evergaol.

Iji became acquainted with Jerren when he was a guest of the Carians. Jerren recalls that the weapons Iji smithed were blunt, yet did not decay when faced with Scarlet Rot. Jerren may also offer a vital clue regarding Ranni's fate, which helps Iji to come to the realisation that General Radahn must be killed in order to release the stars and Ranni's own fate.

Later, after Blaidd breaks free of his imprisonment and gives his life in defence of Ranni, Iji admits that he misjudged Blaidd's loyalty, and senses that he will soon join Blaidd in death. Later, he can be found dead, his body ablaze with black flame, with the corpses of Black Knife Assassins nearby.

infobox.japanese: 魔術教授セルブス (Majutsu Kyōju Serubusu)

npcs.summary: Preceptor Seluvis is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: A preceptor in the service of Ranni the Witch, the last princess of the Carian Royal Family. Seluvis, who resides within a rise in the Three Sisters, openly expresses disdain towards the Tarnished speaking to them with an air of superiority and hostility.

Seluvis was, in the past, acquainted with Gideon Ofnir, however they parted ways due to Dolores, a friend and critique of Gideon's. He was also familiar with Sellen, a sorceress who owes him a favour for assisting her when she was expelled from the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

Seluvis is a collector of "puppets"; living beings transformed into thralls through the administration of a special draught brewed using Starlight Shards. The physical bodies of these puppets are stored in a hidden cellar in the Three Sisters. Among his collection is the body of a sorceress wearing a Witch's Glintstone Crown, into which Sellen's Primal Glintstone can be inserted to provide her with a new body full of vigor.

After becoming acquainted with the Tarnished, Seluvis asks them to give a potion to Nepheli Loux. If Nepheli drinks the potion, she will fall into a deep slumber and become a puppet, with her body residing in Seluvis' basement. Alternatively, if the Tarnished shows the potion to Gideon, he will dispose of it himself and suggest that the Tarnished tell Seluvis that they gave Nepheli the potion. The potion can also be fed to the Dung Eater, resulting in him becoming a Dung Eater Puppet instead.

When the Tarnished confronts Seluvis about his collection of puppets, he offers to brew them their own puppet in exchange for Starlight Shards. If they accept, Seluvis will later task them with retrieving an Amber Starlight, with which he brews an Amber Draught intended to turn Ranni into his puppet. Ranni sees through this treachery, however, and bids the Tarnished leave, killing them if they do not.
Whether the Tarnished aids Seluvis in his betrayal or not, he can later be found dead in his tower, in the same kneeling position as his puppets.

npcs.summary: Rennala is a boss and NPC in Elden Ring. She is a Shardbearer who is encountered in Academy of Raya Lucaria. While this encounter is not required to advance the story, Rennala must be defeated to unlock Moonlight Altar, the ability to respec, and a certain ending.
notes: Rennala is the only boss that not only survives their encounter with the Tarnished but can also be interacted with later as an NPC that allows players to change their appearance or reallocate their stats using her Rebirth magic. The process requires Larval Tears. She is always found in the middle of the Grand Library at the top of the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

When Sellen takes over the Academy, Rennala can still be found in the Grand Library, hiding behind some bookshelves. When Sellen eventually turns into a School of Graven Mages, Rennala is back in her place while Sellen is moved to the side of the library where she remains for the rest of the game.
The approach to the Grand Library which houses Rennala is guarded by Moongrum, one of the last Carian Knights who once served the Lunar Queen.
Rennala would use the Carian Regal Scepter as her Glintstone staff. It is one of the best staffs in the game and it enhances full moon sorceries.

infobox.japanese: 忌まわしき糞喰い (Imawashiki Kusogui)

npcs.summary: The Dung Eater is a serial killer NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: [Background]

The Dung Eater once saw guidance and a ring that would appear at the end of his journey. His vision is of a curse he calls the "pox upon life itself" or the "reviled blessing", with everyone sustaining it in despair and their souls not being able to return to the Erdtree. He decided to wear a disfigured armor, resembling the Omen, representing the vision of the landscape of his mind, and his appearance as he wished to see it. He donned his armor with a heavy sun-shaped medallion to represent both the guidance and the ring he once saw.

He assumed he would personally curse all life himself, so he started indiscriminately killing people and defiling their corpses to nourish the pox. In each defilement, the Dung Eater cultivates a Seedbed Curse on a corpse that prevents the dead soul to go to the Erdtree, leaving it forever cursed.

He was eventually captured and publicly hanged in front of an angry crowd, who strongly despise him for his vile crimes. However, killing the Dung Eater only resulted in his revival by grace as a Tarnished, so he was perpetually jailed in the Forsaken Depths below Leyndell, the Royal Capital.
[Game Events]

When The Tarnished (Protagonist) travels to the Roundtable Hold, an apparition of the Dung Eater is discovered within, resting and with his bloodlust quenched by his abidance of the pact of non-aggression; but should he feel the presence of his Seedbed Curse within the player, he'll instruct to set his body free from the jail hidden away in the sewer below the capital, with the intention of fully cursing The Tarnished.

If The Dung Eater is released, he will attack and defile Blackguard Big Boggart, and will invade the player when they arrive at the scene. When defeated, Dung Eater will claim something unexpected happened, his blessing was warded off by the protagonist, despite the curse stirring within, a feat no one had succeeded in before. At which point he has a revelation: he was not the one who could curse the world as in his vision, that's The Tarnished. And the Dung Eater is just a means to get there, and should be doing what his moniker implies — his flesh is the one that must receive the blessing. And so, he tasks his flesh to be defiled with the seedbed curse again and again until the ring he once saw coalesces and is able to defile Order itself,, an act that would cost his life but that he would be proud of.

The player can choose to follow the Dung Eater's will, defiling his body until a Mending Rune is created, and using it to bring a new age of despair in the end. The Tarnished may also choose to put a stop to his trail of blood by simply killing him in his jail, or to reduce the Dung Eater to a mindless puppet through Seluvis' Potion. Still, perhaps this is a fate too cruel even for a monster like him...

infobox.japanese: 金仮面卿 (Kinkamen-kyō)

npcs.summary: Goldmask is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: Goldmask is a Tarnished scholar and staunch Golden Order fundamentalist. He predicted the guidance of Grace, and upon being beckoned by it he came to the Lands Between to contemplate the Golden Order.

Although a Golden Order fundamentalist himself, Goldmask was critical of the hunters of Those Who Live in Death, lamenting that their learnedness had been reduced to fanatical raving and an obsession with finding a great evil to contend with, a concept which he did not believe existed within the Golden Order.

While contemplating the Erdtree in the Altus Plateau Goldmask is approached by Brother Corhyn, a man of the cloth who wished to travel alongside him as a scholar. In Leyndell, Goldmask becomes perplexed by the identity of Radagon, whose existence calls into question the principle that Queen Marika the Eternal is the one true god. With the help of the The Tarnished, Goldmask learns that Radagon is Marika.

Goldmask and Corhyn then travel to the Mountaintops of the Giants, where Corhyn becomes aware of Goldmask's suspicions regarding the holism of the Golden Order. Corhyn begins to doubt Goldmask's faith, questioning his decision to travel to the Mountaintops.

Goldmask had come to the revelation that the imperfection of the Golden Order and the instability of ideology was due to the fickleness of the gods. After the Erdtree burns, Goldmask returns to Leyndell and dies on the hill near the Erdtree Sanctuary, leaving behind the Mending Rune of Perfect Order, which would allow the Golden Order to be perfected.

npcs.name: Primeval Sorcerer Azur
npcs.summary: Primeval Sorcerer Azur is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: Azur is one of the founding glintstone sorcerers and the originator of the Karolos Conspectus, considered to be the oldest and most venerable lineage of study at the Academy of Raya Lucaria, dedicated to pursuing the mysteries of comets. Azur was Sorceress Sellen's first teacher at the Academy, and she viewed him as a stern judge of character. He glimpsed into the primeval current, where he saw darkness, leaving him both bewitched and fearful of the abyss.

Along with Primeval Sorcerer Lusat, another founding glintstone sorcerer, Azur was driven from the Academy. He settled on Mt. Gelmir, on the outskirts of a Hermit Village populated by Glintstone Sorcerers and Demi-Humans. His body became overrun by blue-green glintstone and he achieved a near-inorganic state, with his glintstone crown replacing his brain and skull.

The Tarnished discovers him on Mt. Gelmir, protected by a group of sorcerers and Demi-Human Queen Maggie. Azur reaches out to the Tarnished and grants them his legendary sorcery, Comet Azur. After revealing Azur's location to Sellen, and subsequently discovering the whereabouts of Lusat, Sellen has the bodies of the two sorcerers moved to the Academy of Raya Lucaria, planning to use them to hone the primeval current.

notes: Azur's Glintstone Staff can be found in the Academy of Raya Lucaria, in a room above the Church of the Cuckoo Site of Grace, guarded by a Noble Page. The room also contains an inactive Graven Mass and a portrait of a woman resembling the Witch's Glintstone Crown.

The Karolos Glintstone Crown resembles a portrait seen in several places in the Academy of Raya Lucaria. As the Karolos Conspectus began with Azur, it is possible that both the portrait and the headpiece are modelled after his original appearance.

npcs.name: Tanith, Volcano Manor Proprietress

infobox.japanese: 火山館の主人、タニス (Kazankan no Shujin, Tanisu)

npcs.summary: Tanith, Volcano Manor Proprietress is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: Tanith is the consort of Praetor Rykard and the leader of the Recusants, a band of Tarnished who have taken up arms against the Erdtree and vowed to hunt down their own kind.

When Tanith first met Rykard, she was working as a dancer in a foreign land, but soon she became his consort. She became truly charmed by Rykard when he swore himself to blasphemy, being the only human to remain by his side when he was devoured by the great serpent, even refusing to imbibe a Tonic of Forgetfulness offered to her by Rykard, believing there to be no greater distress than to forget him.

Tanith is the adoptive mother of Rya, although Rya believes her to be her true mother, having been told that she was born of the grace of a glorious king. Although they are not biologically related, Tanith professes to care for Rya, who's true name is Zorayas.

The Tarnished first meets Tanith in the entrance chamber of Volcano Manor, accompanied by her Crucible Knight bodyguard, where she offers them the opportunity to join the Recusants. Should the Tarnished accept, they are tasked with hunting down several other Tarnished. After tracking down and killing two Tarnished, Tanith divulges the truth about Volcano Manor, and about Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy.

After the Tarnished slays Rykard, Tanith thanks them, as their victory proved Rykard to yet be weak. She announces that she will leave Volcano Manor, however she instead moves to Rykard's audience chamber, where she can be found devouring the corpse of her lord, wishing to become his serpent so that they can devour the gods together.

npcs.name: Gowry

infobox.japanese: 賢者ゴーリー; (Kenja Gōrī)

npcs.summary: Sage Gowry is a merchant NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: Gowry is an elderly sage dwelling in the blighted Caelid Wilds. When the Empyrean Malenia unleashed the Scarlet Rot during her battle with General Radahn, she permanently blighted Caelid. Since that day, Gowry has dedicated himself to her and the Order of Rot he hopes she will usher in.

Gowry found Millicent and her sisters in the Swamp of Aeonia and raised them as his daughters. Seeing them as buds, he sent each of Millicent's sisters to the Haligtree in the hopes that they would bloom into scarlet valkyries.

Millicent became consumed by the Scarlet Rot, and was housed in a church, where she was worshipped by the Pests. Gowry sought the aid of a Tarnished, offering to reveal to them the secret of the magical town of Sellia in exchange for their aid. Gowry bids the Tarnished to journey deep into the Swamp of Aeonia to retrieve a needle of unalloyed gold, which could stem the effects of the Scarlet Rot. After the Tarnished retrieves the needle, Gowry shares the secret of the town, and asks them for another favor; to find Millicent and give her the needle.

Gowry avoids Millicent when she comes to visit his shack, later telling the Tarnished that she has no need of him anymore, and must embark on her fated journey. The Tarnished may aid Millicent on her journey, even giving her a prosthetic arm. Doing so will earn them Gowry's good will, who will offer to teach them a rot incantation, and reveal to them his allegiance to Malenia.

As Millicent travels to the Haligtree, where Malenia awaits, she draws ever closer to her "sisters", who made the same journey as her. Gowry bids the Tarnished to aid the sisters in murdering Millicent, believing that a betrayal by someone she trusts so dearly will cause her to blossom into a flower, which will be reborn as a scarlet valkyrie when Malenia ascends to godhood.

Should the Tarnished kill Millicent, they will return to Gowry's shack to find him seemingly dead. Should they instead aid Millicent against her sisters, she will prevail, but will remove the golden needle, willfully allowing herself to succumb to the Scarlet Rot. The Tarnished may then find Gowry lamenting Millicent's decision, questioning whether she and Malenia detests him and the other children of rot so utterly.

If the Tarnished attempts to kill Gowry, his body will transform into that of a Kindred of Rot. Upon returning to his shack, he will once again resume his human form, revealing that he can inhabit other pests to avoid death.

infobox.japanese: ミリセント (Mirisento)

npcs.summary: Millicent is an NPC cooperator in Elden Ring.
overview: Millicent is a red-haired woman afflicted by Scarlet Rot. She and her sisters were found in the Swamp of Aeonia in Caelid by Sage Gowry, who raised them as his daughters. Her four sisters travelled to Miquella's Haligtree under Gowry's guidance, however Millicent alone remained behind.

At Gowry's behest, the Tarnished obtains an Unalloyed Gold Needle and brings it to the Church of the Plague, where Millicent is slowly succumbing to the Rot. The Tarnished uses the needle to stall the Rot, allowing Millicent to regain lucidity. However, her memories appear to have been affected by her sickness, as when she struggles to remember Gowry upon returning to his shack to find it abandoned.

Millicent sets off on a journey across the Lands Between, retracing the route taken by Malenia, Blade of Miquella after the battle of Aeonia. She once again meets the Tarnished on the Altus Plateau, where they present her with a Valkyrie's Prosthesis to replace her missing sword arm.

Millicent's journey takes her to the Mountaintops of the Giants, in search of a fort containing a medallion which will allow her to access the Haligtree. After the Tarnished claims the medallion and travels to the Consecrated Snowfield, Millicent makes her way to the Haligtree, and to Elphael, the city at its base. Here, she reveals to the Tarnished that she is of Malenia's blood, although she is unsure whether she is a sister, daughter, or offshoot of the Demigod. Unbeknownst to Millicent, however, the Tarnished has been advised by Gowry to assist his remaining four daughters in killing Millicent, so that she can be reborn as a scarlet valkyrie when Malenia ascends to godhood.

The Tarnished may then make a choice: kill Millicent alongside her four sisters, or fight alongside her against the attackers. Should the Tarnished kill Millicent, she will become a scarlet aeonia flower, waiting for Malenia's ascension. If the player fights alongside her, she will remove the needle from her body, allowing her to succumb to the Rot.

npcs.summary: Primeval Sorcerer Lusat is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: Lusat is one of the founding glintstone sorcerers and the originator of the Olivinus Conspectus. He hailed from Sellia, a town of magic-practicing assassins in Caelid. At the Academy of Raya Lucaria, he studied meteors, which formed the basis of the Olivinus Conspectus. He also glimpsed into the primeval current, witnessing the final moments of a great star cluster, the sight of which broke him.

Along with Primeval Sorcerer Azur, another founding glintstone sorcerer, Lusat was driven from the Academy. He returned to his home of Sellia and hid in a cave, protected by a barrier which could only be broken using a Sellian Sealbreaker. In this cave his body became corroded by glintstone as he attained a near-inorganic state, his blue glintstone crown entirely replacing his brain and skull.

After the Tarnished discovers the similarly inorganic body of Azur on Mt. Gelmir and reports his whereabouts to Sorceress Sellen, she entrusts them with a Sellian Sealbreaker and tasks them with tracking down Lusat's body. The Tarnished discovers Lusat, almost immobile and covered in blue crystals, and the sorcerer bestows upon them their legendary sorcery, Stars of Ruin. With both primeval sorcerers located, Sellen has their bodies moved to the Academy of Raya Lucaria, planning to use them to hone the primeval current.

The Olivinus Glintstone Crown resembles a portrait seen in several places in the Academy of Raya Lucaria. As the Olivinus Conspectus began with Lusat, it is possible that both the portrait and the headpiece are modelled after his original appearance.

npcs.name: Finger Maiden Therolina
npcs.summary: Finger Maiden Therolina is an NPC in Elden Ring.

text: Therolina is a Finger Maiden who never met the Tarnished she was meant to guide, even though it was promised that the guidance of grace would ensure that the pair be brought together.

She uses healing incantations and Holy Water Pots, but she is not a fighter by nature and is ill-suited to battle. Nonetheless, she showed up to Radahn's Festival to give a lending hand in felling the demigod.

tables.Spoiler: Her ultimate fate: In the end, she ended up as one of Seluvis' puppets, though it's unknown if this happened before or after the Festival.

tables.Drops: Polite Bow gesture when talked to.

notes: Some believe she was supposed to be the protagonist's Finger Maiden. Nonetheless, our Tarnished can actually see the guidance of grace and the dead maiden that drops the Tarnished's Wizened Finger could be another candidate, implying the player did have a maiden.

npcs.name: Castellan Jerren
npcs.summary: Castellan Jerren is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: Jerren is the elderly castellan of Redmane Castle. In the past, Jerren was a nomadic warrior who became a guest of the Carian Royal Family. There, he became acquainted with General Radahn, the son of Radagon and Rennala, the Carian queen, who would later challenge the stars and arrest their movements, halting fate. He was considered an eccentric by Iji, the blacksmith and war counselor of the Carians. During this time, Jerren made a promise to kill Sellen, a sorceress who had long been a hindrance to the Carians.

After spending time as a guest of the Carians, Jerren served as a guest commander under General Radahn, and the two swore an oath of honourable death to one another. During the Shattering, Radahn fought Malenia, Blade of Miquella in the Battle of Aeonia, and in the aftermath was driven mad by Malenia's rot, cursed to wander the battlefield, devouring the corpses of friends and foes alike. Jerren convened the Radahn Festival to honour his lord, attracting champions from across the Lands Between by promising a battle against the General and a chance to claim his Great Rune.

Among the champions who converge upon Redmane Castle to participate in the festival is a Tarnished who succeeds in defeating Radahn, giving him an honourable death. With Radahn dead, the stars are once again set into motion, and Sellen is dispossessed of her immortality. Finally able to uphold his old promise, Jerren travels to Witchbane Ruins on the Weeping Peninsula, where Sellen is bound by the Academy's shackles. When he arrives, he finds her as a husk, her soul having seemingly already fled. Suspecting Sellen to still be alive somewhere, Jerren continues his hunt, eventually tracking her down to the Academy of Raya Lucaria. He vows to kill her and crush her Primal Glintstone, which facilitated her survival. Should the Tarnished aid him in defeating Sellen, he will thank them before departing, promising to meet them again at the next tournament.

npcs.name: Gurranq, Beast Clergyman

infobox.japanese: 獣の司祭、グラング (Kemono no Shisai, Gurangu)

npcs.summary: Gurranq, Beast Clergyman is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: Gurranq is a hulking, bestial clergyman who resides in the Bestial Sanctum in north-eastern Caelid. Long ago, his terrifying ferocity earned him the name "Death of the Demigods. Presently, he seeks Deathroot, a product of the Rune of Death which spread through the Lands Between following the murder of Godwyn the Golden on the Night of Black Knives. Gurranq consumes Deathroot, although it does not appear to sate him.

Gurranq was assisted in his eradication of the Deathroot by D, Hunter of the Dead, a hunter of Those Who Live in Death. However, D passes this duty onto a Tarnished after noticing their prowess for weeding Deathroot. The Tarnished brings the Deathroot they find throughout the world to Gurranq, and is given access to bestial incantations in exchange. Once they have fed Gurranq all the Deathroot they can find, Gurranq leaves the sanctum. Although still not sated, he realises that he can do no more, and that his appetite will be his sole companion.

When the Tarnished travels to Crumbling Farum Azula to claim the Rune of Death, they encounter Gurranq once more. If the Tarnished had given Gurraq all the Deathroots, he is saddened by his friend's betrayal, but nonetheless attacks the Tarnished to protect the Rune of Death from them. Gurraq is overwhelmed, forcing him to use the Rune of Death to empower himself and reveal his true form as Maliketh, the Black Blade, shadowbound beast of Queen Marika the Eternal. The Tarnished defeats Maliketh, and unleashes the Rune of Death.

npcs.name: Shabriri

infobox.japanese: シャブリリ (Shaburiri)
infobox.aka: The Most Reviled Man in All History

npcs.summary: Shabriri is an NPC in Elden Ring.
overview: Shabriri, the most reviled man in all history, is said to have begun the sickness of the flame of frenzy. He was the first known worshiper of the Three Fingers and the flame of frenzy. For the crime of slander, he had his eyes gouged out. The Three Fingers would later use this opportunity to let the flame of frenzy then fester within his empty sockets.

Shabriri's spirit somehow lives on, able to claim the bodies of others as his own, making them his vessels. The Tarnished encounters Shabriri in the Mountaintops of the Giants, where he is shown to be inhabiting the body of Bloody Finger Hunter Yura. The Tarnished, at the behest of Melina, is bound for the giant's forge so that the maiden may set the Erdtree aflame. However, Shabriri attempts to persuade the Tarnished to seek out the Three Fingers in the depths below Leyndell, revealing that their ascendency to the throne of Elden Lord would require Melina's sacrifice. He proposes an alternative path: the Tarnished may inherit the flame of frenzy and serve as kindling, sparing Melina's life. Shabriri bids the Tarnished become the Lord of Chaos, burning the Erdtree to the ground and incinerating all that divides and distinguishes.
